post.description: Adds the bearer token's jti to the revocation denylist until its own exp, so it cannot be replayed after logout. Revokes only the presented token — the whole session is revoked by Keycloak's back-channel logout callback. Always returns 204, including when no token is presented.

Called by Keycloak, not by clients. Accepts a signed logout token and denylists its session id so every access token minted for that session stops verifying immediately. Unauthenticated by design — the logout token is the credential. See https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-backchannel-1_0.html

logout_token.description: Signed JWT carrying the back-channel logout event and the sid to revoke.

400.description: Missing, unverifiable, or non-conforming logout token

503.description: Revocation store unavailable — the session was NOT revoked

get.description: The calling user's Keycloak profile (name, email, job title, timezone). Needs a Keycloak bearer token; an API key or embed session gets 401 - use whoami for those.

put.description: Partial update: omit a key to leave that field unchanged. `firstName` and `lastName` must be non-blank and contain at least one letter when present — a blank value is rejected rather than clearing the stored name, because omitting the key is already how a caller says 'leave unchanged'. `jobTitle` and `timezone` accept a blank value as a deliberate clear. `email` is immutable here and is ignored. Values are trimmed, truncated to 255 characters, and must contain no control characters, angle brackets or invisible codepoints — the latter class includes characters that render as blank without being whitespace, such as the Hangul fillers and U+2800.

jobTitle.description: Blank clears the stored job title.

timezone.description: IANA zone name. Blank clears the stored timezone.

inviteStatus.description: Whether this person still has an invite outstanding. Derived from the Keycloak VERIFY_EMAIL required action ALONE, not from "has any required action": somebody part-way through a two-factor or passkey setup, or carrying a forced password change, is `accepted` -- they already have access. Consequence worth planning for: `emailVerified: false` can appear beside `inviteStatus: "accepted"`, because accounts created outside the invite paths hold full access without a verified address. Do not treat this field as an email-verification signal. `unknown` means this member's Keycloak profile could not be read at all -- it is NOT a synonym for accepted, and clients must not render it as one.

expiresAt.description: Membership end date, or null for permanent access.

lastName.description: Must not contain <, >, or invisible characters.

role.description: One of owner, admin, developer, operator, viewer, end_user, or a custom role id (cr_...) of the target org.

endOrgId.description: Invite into this tenant of the caller's org.

expiresAt.description: Time-limited access: when the membership stops being valid. Must be in the future and carry a UTC offset. Omit for permanent access.

200.description:
The address already had an account, so it was granted membership rather than created. Same shape as the 201.

`emailSent` is the one field a caller must not skip: the invite and the notification are separate steps, and the membership is committed before the mail is attempted, so `emailSent: false` means this person HAS access and has not been told. It is reported, never assumed -- it reflects what the mail provider said it did with the message, not merely that some upstream request was accepted. It is false too when the sign-in link could not be built into something the identity provider will honour, in which case nothing was sent rather than something unusable. When it is false, `emailNote` carries a sentence to show the admin, and the right UI is to keep them on the screen and tell them to follow up rather than to render success.

201.description:
User invited. Carries `inviteStatus`: `pending` for a brand-new account, and for an address that already had one whatever its real state is -- `accepted` when that person has already verified, so a caller must not assume an invite response means somebody has to act. Whether this person still has an invite outstanding. Derived from the Keycloak VERIFY_EMAIL required action ALONE, not from "has any required action": somebody part-way through a two-factor or passkey setup, or carrying a forced password change, is `accepted` -- they already have access. Consequence worth planning for: `emailVerified: false` can appear beside `inviteStatus: "accepted"`, because accounts created outside the invite paths hold full access without a verified address. Do not treat this field as an email-verification signal.

Also carries `emailSent`, and a caller that reports "invited" without reading it will tell an admin something untrue. See the 200 response for what it means.

400.description: Validation error — includes an expires_at that is not ISO-8601 or is in the past

Accepted at the top level or nested under `config`, and must be a non-blank string of at most 200 characters with no control characters, angle brackets or invisible characters. A value that differs from the current name is a rename and requires org.update; resending the name the org already has is a no-op and needs only settings.update, so a form that posts the name on every save still works. Omit it to leave the name unchanged; a blank value is rejected rather than clearing the saved name. The rename and the config write commit together.

domain.description: Normalised before validation; null clears it. Changing it switches domain auto-join off until re-established.

defaultMemberRole.description: Role a domain-matched joiner gets. admin is accepted only from platform_admin.

Requires connectors.read.

post.description: Creates a connector in the caller's org with its auth methods. Setting visibility to public (listing it in every customer's catalog) is platform_admin only, and connectionVerifyActionId cannot be set until the actions exist (400). 409 when the slug is taken in the org. Requires connectors.create.

409.description: Slug already exists

post.summary: Request a connector the catalog does not carry
post.description:
Records demand for a system fastn has no connector for. Available to anyone who can read the catalog, including an end_user on an embed token, since they are who hits the dead end. Upserts on (org, name): a repeat ask bumps requestCount rather than adding a row, and returns 200 instead of 201.

Only `name` is required. Every qualifying answer is optional at this layer on purpose — the connectors-page form requires three of them, but the one-click surfaces that hit the dead end hardest send a name alone, and rejecting those would exclude exactly the population this exists for.

On a repeat ask every mergeable column is COALESCE(existing, new): the first answer wins and later asks fill only what was still blank. For the prose (note, useCase) that keeps the original account of the problem; for websiteUrl it lets a one-click ask be completed later without being rewritten. Nothing is lost — every ask, repeats included, goes to Slack verbatim.

After the response, and unable to affect it, the write emits the `connector_requested` PostHog event and posts to the connector team’s Slack channel when SLACK_CONNECTOR_REQUEST_WEBHOOK_URL is configured. Neither is reported back — the row is the durable record either way.

Restoring a soft-deleted connector does not bring them back: reconnect. Scoped to the connector's owning org and its tenants; a platform-owned (org_platform) connector cascades nothing, since its connections belong to every customer. For an org migrated to UCL this counts only the legacy rows fastn still holds — the credential itself is UCL's and goes with UCL's own cascade.

Creates (or upserts) a connection. Partner backends select the customer org either via the identity headers (x-org-id + x-user-id, proven with x-identity-hmac when the API key's identity-verification mode requires it) or via orgId/endOrgId in the body (tenant's fastn org id or its external_ref). When identity headers are present, body orgId/userId must agree with the claim. Upserts by name, or by scope when `connectionScope` is set (re-provisioning a scope rotates that row's credentials); `connectionScope` requires a tenant (endOrgId) and must be one of the connector's allowed scopes in the org's SaaS-connector registry.

parameters.description: Which pool. saasPool = the caller's own connections. customers = every child tenant's connections and none of the caller's own (the partner Connections page's customer view) - account-tier roles only, and refused for a tenant-scoped session.

parameters.description: Include the partner's shared pool alongside a customer's own rows.

parameters.name: allOrgs
parameters.description: platform_admin only — span every org.

put.description: Renames a connection, reconnects it with new credentials, or makes it the connector's default (isDefault: true). For a UCL-held connection only those three are supported (400 otherwise). 409 when the new name is already used at the same address. Requires connections.create.

delete.summary: Disconnect — delete a connection and its stored credential
delete.description: The disconnect endpoint. Takes the connection id from GET /api/v1/connections, not a connector id. 404.description: Connection not found (or outside the caller's scope)

get.summary: List the org's SaaS connectors and their allowed connection scopes
get.description: Lists the connectors the caller's org designated as SaaS connectors, with their allowed connection scopes. Requires settings.read.

get.summary: List end customers' scoped connections for a registered SaaS connector
get.description: The customers' connections carrying a connectionScope for this connector, owned by the caller's org, newest first, with the owning customer and how many non-archived installations pin each. Unscoped connections are excluded. Paginated (default 20/page); the response carries pagination.total. Disconnect via DELETE /api/v1/connections/{id}.

put.summary: Designate a connector as a SaaS connector and set its allowed connection scopes
put.description: Admin/owner only (settings.update). connectorId may be the connector's id or its slug; the registration always stores the id. Scopes validate tenant connection creation and drive the widget editor's connection-scope picker.

404.description: Connector not found or not visible to this org

delete.description: Removes the SaaS-connector designation (and its scopes) from a connector of the caller's org. Requires settings.update; 404 when the connector is not designated.

post.summary: Get a usable OAuth access token for a connection
post.description: Returns only the access token — never the refresh token or client secret — refreshing it on demand when the stored token is at or past expiry. Ownership-scoped: callers reach only their own pool's connections (admin/owner additionally their child tenants'). Used by browser surfaces such as the config page's file pickers.

400.description: Connection has no stored credentials or no OAuth access token

404.description: Connection not found (or outside the caller's scope)

get.description: Lists app-event triggers (triggers fired by a connector's events, e.g. a HubSpot contact.created) in the caller's org, newest first, cursor-paginated. Each row carries its ingest webhookUrl and the provider-side subscriptionStatus. Requires events.read.

post.description: Binds workflows to events a connector emits (1-50 events from GET /api/v1/app-triggers/connectors/{connectorId}/events). The connector must have an app registration or a webhook config, otherwise 400. When the connector supports it the provider-side subscription is created too; the response says whether it was attempted and, when it was not, the ingest URL to register by hand. A POLL event makes the trigger a polling trigger. Requires events.create.

201.description: { data: trigger with webhookUrl, subscription outcome }

400.description: Invalid JSON or a body that fails validation

200.description: Trigger with events, routes, webhookUrl, subscriptionStatus

get.description: Returns one app-event trigger: its subscribed events, route bindings, ingest webhookUrl and subscriptionStatus. 404 when the id is not in the caller's org scope.

put.description: Partially updates an app-event trigger. routes and events, when sent, replace the whole list. Requires events.update.

400.description: Invalid JSON or a body that fails validation

404.description: Not found in the caller's org

delete.description: Deletes an app-event trigger, removing its provider-side subscription and polling timer best-effort first. Requires events.delete.

404.description: Not found in the caller's org

post.description: Re-runs the provider subscription for a FAILED/NONE app-event trigger.
Run-now: dispatches the scheduler's routes immediately. The returned eventId lands in the resulting execution's request headers (x-fastn-event-id), closing the trigger-to-execution verification loop.

429.description: Cooldown held — this scheduler was fired within the last SCHEDULER_MANUAL_FIRE_COOLDOWN_MS (10s default). Body is { error: { code: RATE_LIMITED, details: { reason: manual_fire_cooldown }, retryAfter } } with a Retry-After header. Applies per (calling org, scheduler); a fire that then 404s or 400s still consumes the window

parameters.description: Trigger type filter.

parameters.name: health
parameters.description: Computed health filter.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, clamped to 100.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Default newest. oldest cannot be combined with cursor.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: nextCursor from the previous page.

200.description: Pipeline counters plus per-trigger stats, DLQ counts, circuit-breaker state, and the owning installationId / endOrgId (both null for a trigger created outside an installation)

get.description: Health overview of every trigger (webhook, scheduler, app event) in the caller's org: pipeline counters, per-trigger delivery stats, DLQ depth and circuit-breaker state, with a computed health. order=oldest surfaces the longest-waiting triggers and is single-page (a cursor with it is a 400).

200.description: Per-route stats, DLQ entries, circuit-breaker state, computed health

get.description: Health detail for one trigger: per-route delivery stats, circuit-breaker state per route, a page of its dead-letter entries (dlqLimit, max 100, default 20; dlqCursor to page) and the computed health. 404 when the trigger is not in the caller's org.

get.summary: What happened to a trigger's events, end to end
get.description: Each event the trigger received in the window, classified by its workflow runs (including runs of any replay of it) and its dead-letter rows: succeeded first time, recovered (succeeded after a failed run, a retry or a replay), failedRun (a workflow failed and nothing re-ran it), notRun (no run, or its latest attempt is dead-lettered), inProgress. succeeded and recovered are disjoint. The window is the last days x 24 hours. Recomputed every few minutes; refreshedAt says when. Scheduler triggers have no stored events and report zeros.

200.description: { data: { days, totals, daily[], refreshedAt, countOnlyField } } with counts received, succeeded, recovered, failedRun, notRun, inProgress. countOnlyField is the payload key an event needs to be counted, null when every event counts

404.description: Trigger not found in the caller's org

patch.description: Pauses (DISABLED) or resumes (ACTIVE) any trigger by id, whatever its type. Pausing a scheduler also unregisters its timer; resuming registers it again. Requires events.update; 404 when the trigger is not in the caller's org.

put.description: Count only the events whose payload is an object with this top-level key, so a provider's health checks posted to the same webhook stay out of the event figures. Reporting only: the trigger still accepts and routes every event. Null counts every event. A change recounts the trigger's held history: the last day within half an hour, older days over the following hours.

404.description: Trigger not found in the caller's org

post.description: Force-closes every open circuit breaker on the trigger's routes so deliveries resume immediately instead of waiting out the cool-down. Requires events.update. Returns how many routes were reset.

200.description: Failed deliveries with request payload/eventId/routeId, error, attempts

get.description: Lists dead-letter entries in the caller's org: deliveries that exhausted their retries, with the request payload, eventId, routeId, last error and attempt count. Filter by triggerId; cursor-paginated (limit max 100). Requires events.read.

post.description: Queues one dead-letter entry's original payload for re-delivery to its route. Requires events.replay; 404 when the entry is not in the caller's org, 409 when the trigger or the route binding it targeted no longer exists.

get.description: Events the pipeline consumed, newest first, with the outcome each one got: dispatched (enqueued to its route bindings), no_routes (accepted but the trigger has no bindings, so delivered nowhere), dropped (the trigger was deleted or disabled between ingest and consumption), skipped_backlog (a scheduler fire not dispatched because a run it would start is already waiting for a concurrency slot; payload.skipped says which routes and why). Scoped by org_id OR end_org_id; platform_admin reads unrestricted.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: One of webhook, scheduled, manual. Anything else is a 400 rather than an ignored filter.

parameters.name: env
parameters.description: Environment slug (test, live, or a custom one). Events have no environment of their own, so this matches events whose trigger has a route into that environment; a route with no env runs in test. An event whose trigger fans out to two environments is listed under both. A malformed slug is a 400.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-insensitive needle over source, connectorId, id, status and type.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page. Default 20, max 100 — an unparameterised call still gets the 20-row page it always did.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Zero-based row offset. Rows are ordered receivedAt DESC, id DESC so paging cannot repeat or skip rows that share a timestamp.

parameters.name: delivery
parameters.description: Lists the events behind a Reporting (Overview) count. dlq: dead-letter deliveries that will not be retried again (dead, or failed with every retry spent), first failed in [since, until), excluding routes to workflows labelled Internal or Staging. retrying: dead-letter deliveries still due another attempt, of any age unless since/until bound when they first failed. waiting: events received in the last hour, dispatched, with no workflow run yet (since/until are a 400 here). The Overview counts deliveries; this lists the distinct events they belong to, newest delivery first, so an event dead-lettered on two routes is one row. A delivery with no event id, or whose event is no longer kept, has no row. type, triggerId, env and search apply on top; /counts counts the same set. Anything else is a 400.

parameters.name: outcome
parameters.description: Lists the events behind a Reporting (Overview) events or retry number, over the Overview's window (since = window.from, until = window.to, no until when it ends now) and customer. Event numbers: received, first_attempt, recovered, not_processed, in_progress, replayed, replay_succeeded, replay_failed, replayed_from_dlq, rerun_by_hand, event_replay, after_dlq: the events the trigger_event_outcomes rows summed for that number count, by the hour each was received in, classified again when listed (an event whose outcome changed since the rollup's last pass is listed under its new one). Delivery numbers: recovered_by_retry, sent_to_dlq: the distinct events the counted deliveries carried. Every response carries countedAs { unit: events|deliveries, count (the Overview's number), unlisted (deliveries with no event to list), note }. Cannot be combined with delivery. A tenant-scoped session gets 403. Anything else is a 400.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound on receivedAt (with delivery=dlq or retrying, on when the delivery first failed). A malformed timestamp is a 400.

parameters.name: customer
parameters.description: Narrows to one customer, inside the caller's scope. The caller's own org id: its events with no customer on them (with delivery, the dead letters of its own triggers). An end org of the caller: events whose endOrgId is that customer (with delivery=dlq/retrying, the dead letters its triggers hold). Anything else is a 404. A token scoped to an end org may name only that end org.

200.description: { data: Event[], pagination: { total, limit, offset, totalIsLowerBound } } — id, orgId, endOrgId, triggerId, type, source, payload, status, receivedAt (createdAt is an alias). total stops counting at 10000, at which point totalIsLowerBound is true.

400.description: Malformed since, until or env, unknown type, delivery or outcome, outcome with delivery, or since/until with delivery=waiting

404.description: customer is not the caller or one of its end orgs

get.description: Totals for the events list's filter pills, over the whole scoped and filtered set rather than one page. Deliberately ignores ?type= — each count is what that pill would show if it were selected. Capped by the same 10000-row window as the list total, so the pills and the pager cannot report two different numbers for one set.

parameters.name: env
parameters.description: Environment slug; same meaning as on the list.

parameters.name: delivery
parameters.description: Same meaning as on the list; the pills count the events the list shows.

parameters.name: outcome
parameters.description: Same meaning as on the list; data carries countedAs.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Same meaning as on the list.

parameters.name: customer
parameters.description: Same meaning as on the list.

200.description: { data: { total, byType: { webhook, scheduled, manual }, totalIsLowerBound } }

400.description: Malformed since or until, unknown delivery or outcome, outcome with delivery

404.description: customer is not the caller or one of its end orgs

parameters.description: Only events received at or after this ISO 8601 time. Malformed is a 400.

parameters.name: triggerId
parameters.description: Only this trigger's events. trigger_id is accepted as an alias.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Anything else is a 400.

parameters.name: env
parameters.description: Environment slug; matches events whose trigger has a route into it. Malformed is a 400.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-insensitive needle over source, connectorId, id, status and type.

400.description: Malformed since or env, or unknown type

get.description: Counts received events matching the same filters as GET /api/v1/events, without the 10000 cap the list's total carries. Scoped by org_id OR end_org_id; platform_admin counts across all orgs.

Resolves the evt_ id the webhook ingest returned in its 202. replayOf is the event this one replays (POST /api/v1/events/{id}/replay mints a new id), null otherwise; replayedAt is set on an event that was replayed or redelivered from the dead-letter queue.

200.description: The event with its pipeline outcome, replayedAt and replayOf

404.description: Not found or out of scope

get.description: Every delivery of the event that failed, from the dead-letter queue: route, attempts of max, status, whether retries are exhausted, the last error, first failure, last attempt and next retry. A delivery that succeeded first time has no row; the run it started is listed by GET /api/v1/workflows/executions?eventId=.

200.description: Array of attempts, oldest first, at most 50

404.description: Event not found in the caller's scope

post.description: Re-delivers the stored payload through the event's trigger as a NEW event (its own id and row), using the trigger's current routes. A webhook-trigger event re-enters the ingest stream; an app-trigger event is dispatched to its routes; a scheduled or manual event runs the scheduler now, shares Run now's cooldown and, like Run now, also requires events.create. Dispatched with the original's forwarded headers (minus credentials and signatures), so it runs for the same tenant. Counts against the daily event quota. Sets replayedAt on the original (best-effort; null if it could not be recorded).

403.description: Caller lacks events.replay, or events.create for a scheduled/manual event

404.description: Event not found or out of scope

409.description: Nothing to replay into: TRIGGER_NOT_FOUND, TRIGGER_DISABLED, NO_ROUTES, ROUTE_TARGET_GONE (every bound workflow deleted or disabled) or NOT_REPLAYABLE (recorded without a trigger)

429.description: QUOTA_EXCEEDED (daily event quota), or RATE_LIMITED (org ingest budget, or the scheduler was fired within its cooldown; Retry-After set)

parameters.name: deleted
parameters.description: Trash view: return ONLY soft-deleted workflows instead of live ones. Requires workflows.delete (developer and above); never cascades to the parent org. Restore one with POST /api/v1/workflows/{id}/restore.

parameters.name: groupBy
parameters.description: Pass `category` to order the page by category (uncategorised last) so a category's rows are contiguous and a group cannot straddle a page boundary and reappear under a second copy of its own header. Ordering only — it does not filter. The response's `categories` facet carries the per-category totals for the CURRENT filter, across every page.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: Filter by label id. Repeat to narrow: labels AND together, so ?label=a&label=b returns only workflows carrying BOTH. Ids are de-duplicated. Asking for more labels than a workflow can carry (5) is unsatisfiable and returns an empty page rather than a truncated filter. Ids from another workspace match nothing.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter by the status the list shows: active (enabled with a published version), paused (disabled with a published version), unpublished (never published — dev_version 0, so /execute answers 409 WORKFLOW_NOT_PUBLISHED whatever enabled says). The three partition the set. An unrecognised value is ignored rather than rejected, so a stale link narrows nothing instead of failing.

parameters.name: updatedWithin
parameters.description: Only workflows whose updated_at falls inside this window, measured against the database clock. Relative, not an absolute dateFrom: the filter answers "what changed lately", so a shared link still answers it tomorrow. Unrecognised values are ignored.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order the list by a column: name (case-insensitive), status (Active, then Paused, then Not published), latest (the published dev_version, NOT the version save-counter) or updated. Applied in SQL because the list is paged - ordering the returned page would sort a page rather than a table. Omitted, the list keeps its default order (newest created first; most recently deleted first in the trash view). Unrecognised values are ignored.

parameters.name: dir
parameters.description: Sort direction, default desc. Only 'asc' ascends; anything else descends. Ignored without ?sort=. Rows are always tie-broken by id so OFFSET paging cannot repeat or skip a row.

parameters.name: executionTier
parameters.description: Only workflows of this tier. Unrecognised values are ignored.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring match on name, slug and description (first 200 characters).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, 1-200. Without limit or offset every workflow is returned.

get.description: Lists the org's workflows (requires workflows.read). A tenant also sees the parent org's workflows that were installed for it, with code stripped. Paginated only when limit or offset is passed; the response always carries pagination.total.

403.description: The org can read workflow code but not change it (WF-CODE-READONLY) — the platform-admin entitlement workflow.codeEditor.write is off for this org, and create persists code. Also returned with error quota_exceeded (dimension flows_per_tenant, plus current, limit, plan and a message) when the org already holds as many workflows as its plan allows; waiting does not clear it, which is why it is not a 429.

409.description: A workflow with this slug already exists in the org

post.description: Creates a workflow (requires workflows.create). The connector manifest is extracted from `code` and merged with any connectorManifest entries sent. 409 when a live workflow in the org already has the slug; 403 quota_exceeded when the org holds its plan's workflow cap; 403 WF-CODE-READONLY when the org may read but not write workflow code.

get.description: The workspace's category registry, alphabetical. A category is ONE per workflow and decides where that workflow sits in the list — unlike a label, which is many-per-workflow and filters. Capped per workspace by plan (quota dimension workflow_categories: Launch 2, Scale 10, Enterprise 15, or an admin override); `limit` carries the cap, -1 meaning unlimited. workflowCount excludes soft-deleted workflows.

post.description: Names are unique per workspace, case-insensitively. At the cap the request is refused with code WF-CATEGORY-LIMIT. Creates are serialised per workspace by an advisory lock held for the transaction — the counting subquery alone takes no lock under READ COMMITTED, so two sessions at 4 would both read 4 and both insert.

colour.description: Palette token name, one of: chart-1, chart-2, chart-3, brand, success, info, warning, danger

400.description: Validation error, or the workspace is at its plan's category cap (code WF-CATEGORY-LIMIT, with limit)

409.description: A category with that name already exists in this workspace

patch.description: Rename or recolour. At least one of name/colour is required.

colour.description: Palette token name, one of: chart-1, chart-2, chart-3, brand, success, info, warning, danger

404.description: Category not found in this workspace

409.description: A category with that name already exists

delete.description: The workflows in it are NOT deleted — workflows.category_id is ON DELETE SET NULL, so they fall back to Uncategorised. Deleting the thing you organise BY must never delete the things organised.

200.description: Category deleted; its workflows moved to Uncategorised

404.description: Category not found in this workspace

get.description: The workspace's label registry, alphabetical. Labels are per-workspace (org_id) with NO inheritance: a tenant never sees, renames or deletes its partner's labels. usageCount is how many LIVE workflows carry the label — soft-deleted ones are excluded, so the delete warning does not count workflows already in the trash. Capped per workspace by plan (quota dimension workflow_labels: Launch 2, Scale 10, Enterprise 15, or an admin override); `limit` carries the cap, -1 meaning unlimited.

limit.description: How many labels this workspace may define. -1 is unlimited.

post.description: Names are unique per workspace, case-insensitively — creating `TikTok` when `tiktok` exists is a 409, so the registry cannot drift into three spellings of one label.

colour.description: Palette token name, one of: chart-1, chart-2, chart-3, brand, success, info, warning, danger

400.description: Validation error — blank name, or a colour outside the palette — or the workspace is at its plan's label cap (code WF-LABEL-REGISTRY-LIMIT, with limit)

409.description: A label with that name already exists in this workspace

patch.description: Rename or recolour. At least one of name/colour is required.

colour.description: Palette token name, one of: chart-1, chart-2, chart-3, brand, success, info, warning, danger

400.description: Validation error, or neither field supplied

404.description: Label not found in this workspace

409.description: A label with that name already exists in this workspace

delete.description: Removes the label from every workflow carrying it, via ON DELETE CASCADE on the link table. The workflows themselves are untouched — they simply lose the label.

404.description: Label not found in this workspace

put.description: Replaces the workflow's labels wholesale — send the full set, not a delta. Ids are de-duplicated BEFORE the cap is applied, so ["l1","l1"] is one label and is accepted. More than 5 distinct ids is refused with code WF-LABEL-LIMIT and no write. Every id must belong to the caller's workspace. The whole operation runs in one transaction behind a row lock on the workflow, so concurrent calls cannot interleave past the cap.

400.description: More than 5 labels (code WF-LABEL-LIMIT), or an id not in this workspace

post.description: Runs the code in the request body, in the sandbox, without saving it. NOTE this does not run a stored workflow: `code` is what executes, and it is required — see POST /api/v1/workflows/{id}/test to run a saved one. `workflowId` is optional context, used to resolve the same installation (connection pins and inline config) a real dispatch of that workflow would use; it must name a workflow in the caller's org, and 404s if not, so a mistyped id is not mistaken for a successful run. When it is passed and the run succeeds with a non-empty input, that workflow's inputSchema/inputExample are re-derived from the input and testInput/testHeaders are saved as its Test-panel defaults.

workflowId.description: Optional. Runs the body's code in this workflow's installation context. Must exist in the caller's org.

verification.description: Optional. Runs contained: every connector call is mocked unless its `slug.action` is listed in liveReadActions; fastn.db statements run inside a transaction that is rolled back; fastn.state / checkpoint / envConfig writes stay in memory; fetch sends only GET/HEAD/OPTIONS and answers anything else locally; sub-flows, fastn.diff, unified writes and file uploads stop the run. The run is never saved as the workflow's test contract. The response carries a `verification` record: connectorCalls (slug, action, mode, input, ok, error), suppressed side effects, dbStatementsRolledBack, and isolationError when the run was stopped.

liveReadActions.description: `slug.action` keys the caller vouches are reads; only these reach the vendor.

200.description: Run result with logs and trace

400.description: Validation error — `code` missing or not a string

403.description: x-fastn-env named in the body headers is outside the caller's environment pin: a test key (or a token minted with it) may run only 'test', a key made for one environment only that environment and 'test'. The gateway never sees the body, so it is held to the pin here. Code: ENV_NOT_PERMITTED.

404.description: workflowId was supplied but names no workflow in this org

post.description: Runs a saved workflow synchronously in the sandbox. No execution row is recorded, so the run does not appear in execution history or count toward execution quota. That is the ONLY thing it avoids: the workflow's real code runs against real connections, so every side effect is real — fastn.db writes land in your workspace, connector actions hit the live provider, and records are genuinely created. mockMode:true narrows this but does NOT remove it: it routes fastn.connector.* calls to stored stubs, so the provider is not touched. fastn.db writes are unaffected and still land in your workspace — the sandbox db context never sees the flag. On success the tested input becomes the workflow's contract: inputSchema/inputExample are re-derived from a non-empty input, and the input/headers are saved as its testInput/testHeaders defaults.

200.description: Run result with logs and trace

403.description: x-fastn-env named in the body headers is outside the caller's environment pin: a test key (or a token minted with it) may run only 'test', a key made for one environment only that environment and 'test'. The gateway never sees the body, so it is held to the pin here. Code: ENV_NOT_PERMITTED.

get.description: Discovery endpoint: lists existing fastn.state keys for the org so new workflows avoid key collisions.

200.description: State keys with values and last update time

get.description: Discovery endpoint: lists tables in the org's workspace schema, or inspects one table's columns and row count when tableName is passed.

Returns one workflow by id, including its labels (requires workflows.read). A tenant may read a parent-owned workflow only when it was installed for it, and then without its code. 404 when not found or not visible.

403.description: Only when the body carries `code`: the org can read workflow code but not change it (WF-CODE-READONLY). A rename, description or enable-toggle that sends no `code` is unaffected.

put.description: Partial update of a workflow (requires workflows.update): only the fields sent are changed. `documentation` is rejected with 400; send documentationOverride to edit the partner-facing doc. A body carrying `code` is refused with 403 WF-CODE-READONLY when the org may read but not write workflow code. Changing only enabled, categoryId or documentationOverride does not bump the version.

delete.description: Soft-deletes by default: the row is retained with deleted=true, stays listable via GET /api/v1/workflows?deleted=true, and is restorable via POST /api/v1/workflows/{id}/restore. It stops being executable immediately (/execute filters deleted=false), so any live trigger routing to it stops delivering — a trigger whose every route points at trashed workflows answers 404 ROUTE_TARGET_GONE instead of 202 until one is restored. Pass permanent=true to drop the row and its executions irreversibly.

parameters.name: permanent
parameters.description: Hard-delete the workflow and its executions. Not restorable.

409.description: Workflow has in-flight executions

post.description: Undoes a non-permanent deleteWorkflow: clears deleted/deleted_at so the workflow is executable and listable again. Any trigger still routing to it resumes delivering on the next fire. Note: while the workflow was in the trash its webhook URL answered 404, so a sender that de-registered the endpoint during that window will not resume on its own and must be re-subscribed on the provider side. Returns { restored: false, reason: 'not_deleted' } when the workflow was never deleted. Requires workflows.delete. Note that unlike the ?deleted=true trash view, this route does not downgrade end_user, and end_user holds workflows.delete in the RBAC matrix - so a tenant end_user can restore its own workflows.

409.description: The slug is no longer free. A workflow created under it while this one sat in the trash owns it now, so clearing `deleted` would collide on idx_workflows_org_slug. Rename or delete the holder, then retry. `conflict` names it.

get.description: The workflow's connector manifest: one entry per connector its code calls, carrying the tenancy scope, the connection pin, the per-connector retry/timeout override, and the action entries with their version pins.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Workflow id (wf_*)

patch.description: Tunes ONE connector entry: tenancy scope + connection pin, the connector-level retry/timeout override, and per-action overrides. The surgical counterpart to PUT /workflows/{id}, which replaces the whole manifest array and so requires the caller to read and echo back every other entry. Applied as a partial at the FIELD level: an omitted field is left untouched, an explicit null clears that override so the entry inherits the connector row again, and at least one settable field must be present. A retryPolicy that is sent REPLACES the stored override rather than merging into it — merging would leave no way to remove a field from a stored layer. Identity fields (slug, connectorId, orgId, action id/version) are not settable — the code extractor owns them, and repointing one here would desync the manifest from the code it describes.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Workflow id (wf_*)

parameters.name: slug
parameters.description: The manifest connector slug OR the connectorId — slug matched first, connectorId second. Matched against this workflow's manifest only, not the connector catalog.

200.description: Entry patched; returns the full manifest after the write

slug.description: The entry's slug, even when it was addressed by connectorId

400.description: Empty patch (no settable field present); connectionId sent alone on a non-SAAS entry; a value outside the schema bounds; invalid JSON

404.description: Workflow not found, connector absent from the manifest (knownSlugs + knownConnectorIds), or an action absent from the entry (knownActionSlugs)

get.description: Returns the workflow's stored documentation for one audience. audience=end_user (default) is the operator-facing help-center doc plus flow-step and sequence artifacts; audience=technical is the solution-engineer doc covering connector actions used, the input/output contract, and reliability behavior. format=structured (default) additionally returns the workflow's live contract (triggers, connector actions, schemas, execution settings) so partners can re-render the content into their own help center; format=markdown returns just the doc text with freshness metadata. Every response carries generatedAt and a stale flag (true when the workflow changed after the doc was generated).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Workflow id (wf_*) or slug

sections.description: The doc split into its H2 sections (heading null = the H1 preamble) — a derived view of markdown for template-based renderers

fieldMappings.description: The Field mapping table as data; [] when the doc has no parseable table — a convenience view, markdown stays canonical

404.description: Workflow not found, or that audience's doc has not been generated yet. The latter carries a hint plus lastGeneration - the outcome of the most recent generation attempt for that audience ({ status: 'ok' | 'failed', at, error? }), or null when no attempt has been recorded. Generation is fire-and-forget behind a 202, so this is how a caller tells 'still running' from 'failed' rather than polling the 404 forever.

get.description: Every doc generation and every override save appends a version row (capped per workflow/audience/kind), so a bad regeneration is diffable and revertible. Returns metadata only, newest first; fetch one version's full content via /docs/history/{versionId}.

Returns one saved documentation version (generated or override) with its full content (requires workflows.read). The workflow may be named by id or slug. 404 when the workflow or version is not found.

post.description: Fire-and-forget regeneration of the workflow's stored documentation from its current code, triggers, schemas, and connector actions. audience=end_user (default) rewrites the operator-facing doc and its visual artifacts; audience=technical writes a spec-only technical document under documentation.technical without touching the end-user doc. A generation that comes back empty is discarded and the previously saved doc is kept.

400.description: Workflow has no code or invalid audience

post.description: Behaviour depends on the workflow's executionTier, and callers must handle both. STANDARD and LONG queue the run and return 202 with an executionId to poll. INSTANT runs synchronously and returns 200 with the finished result — it holds the HTTP request for the duration, which is the point of the tier, so there is nothing to poll. On the instant path the id appears ONLY in the X-Execution-Id response header — the body is the workflow's own return value and has nowhere to put it — so use that header to correlate a synchronous run. The queued path does not set that header; its id is in data.executionId. A caller written to poll unconditionally will break on an instant-tier workflow. An instant timeout on a workflow with escalateOnTimeout also returns 202, naming the escalated standard run in escalatedTo/escalatedFrom. Send Idempotency-Key to make a retry safe: a duplicate returns the existing execution for the same tenant instead of running again — 200 once it has finished, 202 while it is still in flight — and resolves to the escalated run where a timeout escalated.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-supplied dedup key. Scoped to the execution's (owner org, end-org); no expiry window beyond the execution's retention. The prefix fastn-event: is reserved for trigger dispatch and is refused with 400 (reserved_idempotency_key); keys with it replay only an in-flight or completed run from the last 24 hours. Rarely, concurrent requests under one key are answered 503 (idempotency_key_contended) with nothing created; retry. A fastn-event: key whose run exists but was not yet handed to an engine is answered 409 (dispatch_run_not_started); retry.

parameters.name: x-fastn-env
parameters.description: Which environment to execute against, and therefore WHICH CODE RUNS. 'test' runs the workflow's latest published version; any other slug runs the version actively deployed to that environment. Omitted, it defaults to the credential's own mode: a fsk_test_ key gets 'test', a fsk_live_ key gets 'live'. A test key may ONLY name 'test' — asking for anything else is refused with 403 ENV_NOT_PERMITTED rather than quietly downgraded, so a 200 always means the environment you asked for is the one that ran. A live key pinned to an environment (workflowEnvId) defaults to that environment, may also name 'test', and is refused for any other. A live key made before keys were pinned may name any environment, including 'test'.

200.description: Instant tier only — the run finished synchronously and this IS the result. No polling. The executionId is in the X-Execution-Id response header.

X-Execution-Id.description: Id of the run just completed, for correlating logs and traces.

202.description: Standard and long tiers — the run was queued. Poll GET /api/v1/workflows/{id}/executions/{executionId} for the result — the workflow id is part of the path. No X-Execution-Id header on this path; read data.executionId.

escalatedFrom.description: Instant execution whose timeout triggered the escalation

403.description: The credential may not execute against the requested x-fastn-env. A test-mode API key is pinned to the 'test' environment; use a live key to target a deployed environment. Code: ENV_NOT_PERMITTED.

404.description: No active deployment exists for the requested environment. The workflow has been published but never deployed there — deploy a version to that environment, or call with x-fastn-env: test to run the latest published version.

408.description: Instant tier only — the run exceeded its timeout. Carries executionId and durationMs.

409.description: The workflow has no published version at all, so there is nothing to run. Publish a snapshot, or use POST /api/v1/workflows/{id}/test to run the draft. Code: WORKFLOW_NOT_PUBLISHED.

413.description: The workflow returned a result larger than WORKFLOW_MAX_RESULT_BYTES (default 8 MiB). The run is recorded as failed with errorCategory 'configuration' and no output is stored - the oversized result is rejected, never truncated. Return a summary, paginate the response, or write the data to storage and return a reference to it.

get.description: Org-wide execution list, newest first. eventId/triggerId match the x-fastn-event-id / x-fastn-trigger-id headers stamped by the event pipeline on every dispatch, so a trigger fire can be correlated to its execution in one query. sort=duration lists finished runs slowest first and needs dateFrom within 30 days of dateTo (400 otherwise). List rows are metadata: they omit input, output, logs and trace (hasTrace flags a trace), and requestHeaders carries only x-fastn-event-id / x-fastn-trigger-id; outputCounts reports the run's record counts. Fetch a run's bodies from the per-execution detail route.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Comma-separated statuses; matches any of them.

parameters.name: parentExecutionId
parameters.description: Only the sub-flow runs this execution started (fastn.flow.invoke, invokeAsync, map); each row's parentExecutionId names its parent. Still inside the caller's org scope. Present but empty matches nothing rather than every execution.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-insensitive match against workflow name/slug, execution id, status, triggered-by, error category, and the dispatched event and trigger ids.

parameters.name: searchIn
parameters.description: payload also matches search against each run's input body, e.g. a record id the sender put in a webhook, as a WHOLE value (75073605 does not match 1750736050). Ids are matched whole too, and workflow names by substring. Requires workflows.execute (403 otherwise), a search of at least 3 characters, and a dateFrom no more than 7 days before dateTo (or now); anything else is a 400. Applies to /workflows/executions/counts too.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: duration lists finished runs slowest first; it needs dateFrom within 30 days of dateTo (400 otherwise). Omitted, newest first.

200.description: Execution list rows with workflow name/slug/version/tier. Any `search` walks the window newest-first within a time budget and also returns `payloadSearch: { complete, searchedFrom, hasMore, unsearched }` (the name predates ordinary searches using it): `complete: false` with `hasMore: false` means it stopped at `searchedFrom` before reaching dateFrom. `unsearched` counts runs whose input is archived to GCS but too large to search (0 almost always). With a `search`, `pagination.total` is a floor (`totalIsLowerBound`), and with no dateFrom the search covers the last 90 days, the longest any run is retained. /workflows/executions/counts with a `search` caps at 1000 matches and sets isLowerBound.

400.description: dateFrom/dateTo is not an ISO 8601 date or date-time (VALIDATION_ERROR), or searchIn=payload without a short enough window or a long enough search

403.description: searchIn=payload from a role that cannot read execution bodies

get.description: The fastn.loki and mirrored console.* lines of every run the caller can see, read from Grafana Loki: the newest `limit` matches, returned oldest first. Every line's run is re-checked against the executions the caller may read, and a line whose run is not visible is dropped, so `lines` can be shorter than `limit` while `truncated` is true. With `since` (the previous answer's `cursor`) it is a live-tail poll: the newest lines from 15s before that cursor, so lines that reached Loki late are not lost; drop the ones already shown. `since` is clamped inside the dateFrom/dateTo window, so it can never widen the search, and one past dateTo answers no lines. `cursor` is the newest line Loki answered (visible or not), never behind `since`, and with no lines the end of the window on the server's clock. The run-end line each run writes (`source: fastn.run`, Loki label `status`) is not returned. Lines are kept for Loki's retention (14 days on the run-logs instance), not the run's. Requires workflows.execute to see lines: other roles get 200 with `available: false, reason: redacted`. Loki unset or failing is 200 with `available: false` and a reason.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive text matched literally against the whole line, message and logged data alike.

parameters.name: dateFrom
parameters.description: Default: one hour before dateTo. At most 7 days before dateTo.

parameters.name: dateTo
parameters.description: Default: now.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Live tail: the previous answer's cursor (nanoseconds). Clamped to the window.

200.description: `{ source: 'loki', available, reason?, lines: [{ ts, tsNs, level, source, message, executionId, workflowId, data }], truncated, runs: { <executionId>: { workflowId, workflowName, status } }, cursor }`

400.description: A window over 7 days or ending before it starts, an unknown level, a malformed since, or a limit outside 1-1000 (VALIDATION_ERROR)

get.description: Execution history of one workflow, newest first (requires workflows.read). limit is capped at 100; a non-integer limit, offset or status_code is a 400.

200.description: Execution detail. `bodiesSource` says where input, request headers, output, logs and trace came from: `gcs` when the run's archived bundle was read (EXECUTION_BODIES_READ_FROM=gcs and the run has one), `postgres` otherwise.

get.description: One execution with its steps, logs and trace (requires workflows.read). Log and trace bodies are omitted for roles that cannot read execution bodies. 404 when the run is not in the caller's scope.

delete.description: Marks a pending, queued or running execution cancelled and stops its engine run (requires workflows.execute). A finished run is left unchanged; the response is still 200.

404.description: Execution not found in the caller's scope

get.summary: Get an execution's log lines from Loki
get.description: The run's fastn.loki lines and mirrored console.* lines, read back from Grafana Loki: the most recent `limit` lines, returned oldest first. A run past its hourly shipping budget (5000 lines an hour) has a warn line for each hour it dropped lines, saying how many. Scoped exactly like the execution detail route. Lines an inline sub-flow (fastn.flow.invoke) wrote are included, each naming its own executionId. Never a 5xx for Loki trouble: when Loki is not configured (LOKI_QUERY_URL unset) or the query fails the answer is 200 with available: false and a reason, and the run's stored console lines remain on the detail route. A role without workflows.execute gets available: false, reason: redacted, as for every other run body.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Lines to return. Absent or blank uses the default; anything outside 1-5000 is a 400.

200.description: Log lines, or why there are none

source.description: Where this answer came from. Always loki: this route reads nothing else. The run's stored console lines (Postgres) are only on the execution detail route, under data.logs.

truncated.description: True when the page is full: the run has older lines than these, which Grafana still holds.

data.description: The data object passed to fastn.loki, if any.

400.description: `limit` is not a whole number between 1 and 5000

404.description: Execution not found in the caller's scope

post.description: Re-runs a finished execution with its original input, request headers and tenant/installation binding, at the tier that run actually used rather than the workflow's currently configured tier. Runs the current code for the resolved environment (x-fastn-env / ?env=), since executions do not record the version they ran. Refuses a run that is still pending/queued/running (409), and a run whose installation is no longer active (409). Instant-tier replays return 200 once the run finishes, with its outcome in the body; standard/long return 202 with the new executionId to poll.

404.description: Execution, workflow, or environment deployment not found

409.description: Run still in flight, or its installation is no longer active

get.description: Sync run reports written by fastn.diff (per-run created/updated/deleted/unchanged stats plus capped field-level change details), read from the org's workspace schema.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Logical baseline key (e.g. hubspot-company-sync)

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Only reports created before this instant (keyset paging)

get.description: The org's workflow environments, ordered default first, then oldest first, then by id as a tiebreak (environments created together in one bulk call share a creation timestamp, so id is what makes the order total). Includes the built-in Live environment (slug 'live', isDefault true, isDeletable false), which every workflow-authoring org is seeded at creation — it is a real row, and its id is what /workflows/{id}/deploy and /workflows/{id}/promote accept. A customer workspace (end_org) is deliberately not seeded one and can legitimately return an empty list. 'test' is a separate hardcoded environment with no row here; it is a valid env_slug for env-configs only, never a deploy target.

post.description: Creates a custom (non-default, deletable) environment for the caller's org. The slug is lowercased; every character outside [a-z0-9-] is replaced with '-' one-for-one (hyphens are preserved and runs are NOT collapsed, so 'a  b' becomes 'a--b'); then leading and trailing hyphens are stripped, which is why 'live!' normalizes to 'live' and is rejected as reserved. 'test' and 'live' are both reserved and rejected with 400: 'test' has no row at all, and 'live' is the built-in production environment seeded at org creation, which this route would otherwise create with custom-env flags.

400.description: Missing name/slug, or a reserved slug

409.description: An environment with that slug already exists in this org

patch.summary: Toggle review gating for an environment
patch.description: Sets requiresReview. When true, /workflows/{id}/deploy refuses the environment with a 409 and the caller must use /workflows/{id}/promote, which opens a real PR against the org's connected GitHub repo.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Environment id (wenv_*)

404.description: No such environment in the caller's org

400.description: The built-in Live environment cannot be deleted

404.description: No such environment in the caller's org

delete.description: Deletes a custom workflow environment (requires workflows.delete). The built-in Live environment cannot be deleted (400). 409 ENVIRONMENT_HAS_API_KEYS while an active API key is pinned to it; 403 ENV_NOT_PERMITTED for an API key pinned to a different environment.

get.summary: Get one published version, with its code
get.description: Returns one immutable published snapshot (wv_*) of the workflow, including its code. The version list omits code; this is how a caller reads what a deployment runs, by the versionId from GET /workflows/{id}/deployments. A tenant reading a workflow its partner owns gets 404, as the workflow read strips code for that caller. Requires workflows.read.

post.summary: Deploy a published version to an environment
post.description: Deploys a published workflow version (wv_*) to one environment. env_id must be a wenv_* id belonging to the caller's org — the environment slug is not accepted. Deploying to the default environment also updates the workflow's live code pointer. An environment with requiresReview set is refused here; use /promote.

403.description: The org can read workflow code but not change it (WF-CODE-READONLY). Deploying to the default environment rewrites the live code pointer, so it is refused for a read-only org.

404.description: Environment not found in this org, or version not found for this workflow

409.description: Environment requires review — use /promote

post.description: Deploys a published version to an environment, taking one of two branches depending on that environment's requiresReview flag. requiresReview false (the DEFAULT, and the state of every built-in Live environment — ensureLiveEnvironment does not set the flag): this is a bit-for-bit passthrough to /deploy. It deploys immediately, opens no PR, writes no promotion record, and — because Live is the default environment — updates the workflow's live code pointer. There is no review step despite the operation name. requiresReview true: opens a PR against the org's connected GitHub repo and records a pending promotion; the deploy runs when that PR is merged. The 200 body differs per branch (see the response schema). env_id must be a wenv_* id belonging to the caller's org, obtained from GET /api/v1/environments; a slug is not accepted. Requires workflows.deploy_prod when the target is the default (Live) environment, workflows.deploy_test otherwise.

200.description: Deployed immediately (requiresReview false), or promotion opened (requiresReview true) — the two branches return different shapes

oneOf.title: Deployed
oneOf.description: requiresReview false — the passthrough branch, identical to POST /workflows/{id}/deploy

oneOf.title: PromotionOpened
oneOf.description: requiresReview true — awaiting a merged GitHub PR

400.description: env_id or version_id missing; or, on the review branch, no GitHub repository connected for this org, or the GitHub App is not configured on this platform

403.description: The org can read workflow code but not change it (WF-CODE-READONLY). Promote goes through the same deploy mechanism that rewrites the live code pointer, so it is refused for a read-only org.

404.description: Environment not found in this org, version not found for this workflow, or workflow not found

409.description: A promotion is already awaiting review for this workflow and environment

get.description: Lists the org's sync jobs, newest first (requires workflows.read).

post.description: Creates an active sync job for a connector entity (requires workflows.create). direction defaults to inbound; the name is derived from connectorId and entity.

get.description: Returns one sync job (requires workflows.read). 404 when it is not in the org.

delete.description: Deletes a sync job (requires workflows.delete). 404 when it is not in the org.

post.description: Runs the sync engine for the job synchronously (requires workflows.execute) and returns the updated job with syncResult (processed, failed, skipped, errors).

Unauthenticated by design — a violation report carries no credentials and is often sent from a page whose scripts were just blocked. Answers 204 to everything, including a malformed body: the browser cannot act on an error and a parse failure must not register as an application 4xx. Reports are sanitised (query strings and fragments stripped from every URI before logging) and logged, not stored. post.summary: Fork (duplicate) an inherited integration into your own org so you can customise it
post.description: For a child org (a tenant) whose parent offers an integration (widget) it wants to change. The parent's integration can never be modified from a child org; this copies it into the caller's org and the copy is fully the caller's to edit. Copies the widget, its config template, every workflow it runs (lifecycle hooks, trigger targets, config option sources and every sub-flow they invoke, published, and deployed wherever the source is live), everything those workflows read by org at run time (env config values, secrets, the configs they name, the environments they run in), their category, labels, documentation and validation, its trigger templates (webhook, schedule and app-event, routed to the copied workflows, with the webhook configs and app registrations app events need) and the parent's CUSTOM connectors with their actions, auth methods, entities, mock stubs and OAuth providers including client secrets. Catalog connectors are shared by every org and stay referenced; so do all connectors when the caller's role cannot author connectors (end_user) - the response lists them in sharedConnectorIds. Every id is rewritten so the copy points at the copies. The parent's integration stays where it is and existing installations of it keep running. The customer sees ONE integration with two versions, their copy and the original: the copy becomes the active version, unless they already run the original, which then stays active until they switch (setWidgetActiveVersion). Idempotent: forking again returns the existing copies (200), and a fork that failed part-way resumes when repeated. Pass ?endOrgId=<tenant> from a partner session to fork into that tenant. Use it when the caller wants to change an integration whose orgId is not their own org; ask them first. Afterwards change ONLY the copies named in data.items (type workflow: updateWorkflow or editWorkflowCode, then publishWorkflow, then run it), never the original ids. Tell the caller which connectors stay shared (sharedConnectorIds) and relay warnings. A copy deployed to live keeps running the previous version for live traffic until it is deployed again. If the customer already has a copy (a widget in listWidgets with version.kind = custom), change THAT copy; forking again returns it. If the original is still their active version, offer to switch (setWidgetActiveVersion): switching pauses their setup on the original and moves it to the copy with the same connected accounts.

get.description: Who you are talking to. Answers from the gateway's resolved context, so it works for every credential a caller can arrive with — a dashboard JWT, an API key, an embed (widget) token and a share link alike; unlike GET /api/v1/profile, which reads the Keycloak user and is therefore unavailable to an embed session. Call it before your first substantive reply and adapt to the answer. Two independent axes, and do not collapse them: `actor` is WHICH CREDENTIAL, `actingAsTenant` is WHOSE WORKSPACE. `actingAsTenant: true` means the credential was minted for a tenant of a parent org — `org` is that customer's own workspace and `parentOrg` is the partner whose product they are using — so speak in business terms about their own connections and not about building the platform. Their provider's integrations are theirs to use, and to customise by forking a copy into their own workspace (forkIntegration) - never in place. It is true for a partner's customer in an embedded widget AND for a tenant-scoped API key, so it does not on its own mean a human is present; read `actor` for that. `actingAsTenant: false` means the caller is acting as the org itself, which for `actor: user` is the partner's own staff in the dashboard, with `role` naming the persona. `permissions` reports three layers rather than one merged list, because enforcement is a layered predicate and a merged copy would drift from it: `role` is the enforced baseline for the persona, `structured` overrides it when present (for a custom-role member it IS the effective set, already intersected against the base role), and `apiKeyGrant` is a ceiling over both and never widens them. Retired-resource entries may appear in `role` and govern nothing. Every tool call you make executes under this identity, so a 403 means this persona lacks the permission rather than a fault worth retrying. One limitation: a caller whose token carries no org claim at all is answered 401 rather than a partial identity, which in practice means a platform_admin holding no org_id — the same guard every other /api/v1/me/* read uses.

post.summary: Research a SaaS company by domain
post.description: Web research on a SaaS company from its domain (e.g. hubspot.com): company profile, existing integrations, customer pain from reviews and communities, competitors, integration gaps, customer tool ecosystem, business opportunity, named customers, recent news, and the product's own API (docs, OpenAPI spec, base URL, auth, core data objects, webhook events). Returns a markdown summary, per-topic JSON (results), source URLs, and profile: a normalised product profile (company, api, entities, webhooks with use cases, existing and suggested integrations, an example first integration). progress lists four steps (website, api_docs, entities, webhooks) with status and a short finding each. Results are cached per domain for 30 days: if the domain was researched in that time, the full report comes back immediately with status "ready"; an older one, or one researched before profiles existed, is re-run. Otherwise a run starts (about 1-3 minutes; profile usually arrives first, with progress.profileReady) and the response is 202 with status "running" and id = the domain; call getSaasResearch with that domain every pollAfterSeconds until status is "ready" or "failed". refresh=true forces a new run and returns the previous report marked stale while it runs. Public email domains (gmail.com etc.) are a 400. A 402 means the org is out of AI credits; getSaasResearch still returns a cached report for the domain without spending any. Roles: owner, admin, developer, operator.

202.description: { data: { status: 'running', id, domain, pollAfterSeconds, progress: { steps, tasks, profileReady }, profile?, stale?, ...previousReport } }

400.description: Invalid body, not a hostname, or a public email domain

bearerAuth.description: A Keycloak access token. Which org the request runs as depends on the client the token was minted for (its azp). A dashboard session follows the dashboard's org picker: a fastn-admin token, or a fastn-app token on a request carrying the x-fastn-dashboard header that the dashboard adds to every call. A fastn-app token without that header (for example one minted by username/password from a script) is treated like any other client. Any other client (the UCL/MCP gateway, CLIs, service accounts) never follows the picker: it runs in the org named by the x-fastn-target-org header, or, without the header, in the user's home org — for a platform_admin their platform org, otherwise the oldest company/partner org they own, else the oldest company/partner org they belong to, else their personal org. Failures on a non-dashboard session: 400 with code invalid_target_org when x-fastn-target-org is not shaped like an org id; 403 with code org_not_member when the user holds no active membership in the org it names. POST /api/v1/users/me/switch-account answers 409 switch_account_dashboard_only for a non-dashboard session, because the picker does not steer it.

XFastnTargetOrgHeader.name: x-fastn-target-org
XFastnTargetOrgHeader.description: JWT sessions from a non-dashboard client (UCL/MCP, CLI, service account) only: the fastn org id to act in, for users who belong to more than one org. Without it such a session runs in the user's home org (see bearerAuth). Ignored on dashboard sessions, which follow the org picker, and never forwarded past the gateway. 400 invalid_target_org when malformed; 403 org_not_member when the user holds no active membership there. Not the partner x-org-id header, which is for API keys and names a customer org.

XInstallationIdHeader.name: x-installation-id
XInstallationIdHeader.description: Installation whose widget config values (unifiedValues) apply to this call. Omit for a call with no widget identity.

XOrgIdHeader.name: x-org-id
XOrgIdHeader.description: Customer org the request acts for — the tenant's fastn org id or the external_ref the partner registered it under. Requires API-key auth on a multi-tenant key; always ownership-checked against the key's account. When the key's identity-verification mode is not off, must be proven with x-identity-hmac.

XUserIdHeader.name: x-user-id
XUserIdHeader.description: End-user identifier the partner's backend authorized for this request. May accompany x-org-id or stand alone; covered by x-identity-hmac when the key enforces identity verification.

XIdentityHmacHeader.name: x-identity-hmac
XIdentityHmacHeader.description: Hex HMAC-SHA256 of "{x-org-id}\n{x-user-id}" (the header values exactly as sent, newline-joined; an absent header is the empty string) signed with the API key's identity-verification secret. Required when the key's idv mode is 'required' (missing/invalid = 401); logged-only under 'optional'; ignored when 'off'.

retryPolicy.description: Retry behaviour for the WORKFLOW RUN itself — not the connector-call retry policy on connectorManifest[].retryPolicy, which is a different shape (initialDelayMs/backoffMultiplier/maxDelayMs) and IS fully honoured. `maxAttempts` is total attempts INCLUDING the first, and defaults to 1 — so retry is opt-in and a workflow that declares no policy runs exactly once. On `standard`/`long` it bounds Cloud Run task retries (`shouldRetryBatchTask`), which fire for a retryable failure: a transient SystemError (a platform fault, or a dropped or timed-out database connection), a timeout, a 5xx the workflow RETURNED, or a connector 5xx/408/425/429 that escaped user code. A deliberate `throw` in user code, code that does not compile, a 4xx, an out-of-memory and a cancellation are deterministic and never retry. Attempts RESUME rather than re-run: the executionId is unchanged, so `ctx.isRetry` + `fastn.checkpoint` continue where the last attempt stopped. `initialIntervalMs` / `backoffCoefficient` / `maximumIntervalMs` are honoured as an in-task sleep before a re-run, which is billable and comes out of the run's own timeout. On `instant` it bounds an in-process re-run loop that retries the same failures as the async tiers, and only when the run is not tier-escalation-eligible (escalateOnTimeout forces a single attempt). The loop discards the previous attempt rather than resuming it, honours the interval fields between attempts, and stops early when the next attempt cannot fit the tier's ~25s gateway budget — so a connector failure whose own retries already spent that budget gets no further attempt. Same declared number, resume semantics on one tier and re-run semantics on the other. See docs/services/WORKFLOWS.md.
